title: Understanding and Using Light and Sound
seo_title: Grade 11 General Science: Understanding and Using Light and Sound Worksheets (Strengthened SHS)

standard_text: Understanding and using light and sound: reflection, refraction and lenses; the electromagnetic spectrum; sound waves, echoes and ultrasound; applications in technology and medicine. (summary of the Strengthened Senior High School curriculum, General Science, Term 1)
meta_desc: Free Grade 11 General Science worksheets (Strengthened SHS curriculum, Term 1): reflection, refraction and lenses, the electromagnetic spectrum, sound and echoes, and ultrasound. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Light can be reflected and refracted.
key_sub: Sound needs a medium; light does not.
body_html:
How to think about it

Light travels in straight lines at 3 × 10⁸ m/s. It reflects from mirrors (angle of incidence = angle of reflection) and refracts when it enters a different medium, which is how lenses in eyeglasses, cameras and microscopes work.

Sound is a longitudinal wave that needs a medium. Echoes are reflected sound; sonar and ultrasound use echoes to measure distances and to see inside the body. Noise can damage hearing, so loud sounds should be limited.

Example

Angle of incidence 35°. Angle of reflection?

Law of reflection

Answer: 35°

Example

An echo returns after 1 s (sound 340 m/s). Distance to the wall?

Half of 340 m

Answer: 170 m

Common mistakes

  • Measuring angles from the mirror instead of the normal.
  • Thinking sound travels through a vacuum.
  • Forgetting to halve the distance in echo problems.

faq.q: Why does a spoon look bent in a glass of water?
faq.a: Light refracts as it passes from water to air.
Echoes of high-frequency sound make images of babies and organs.

items.q: A ray strikes a plane mirror. The angle between the ray and the normal is 20°. What is the angle of reflection?
items.e: Angle of reflection = angle of incidence = 20° (both measured from the normal).

items.q: The angle of reflection at a plane mirror is 25°. What is the angle between the reflected ray and the mirror surface?
items.e: The normal is at 90° to the mirror, so the angle is 90° − 25° = 65°.

items.q: A ray strikes a plane mirror. The angle between the ray and the normal is 55°. What is the angle of reflection?
items.e: Angle of reflection = angle of incidence = 55° (both measured from the normal).

items.q: The angle of incidence on a plane mirror is 50°. What is the angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray?
items.e: The angle between them is i + r = 50° + 50° = 100°.

items.q: A ray of light enters a block from air with an angle of incidence of 25° and an angle of refraction of 10°. What is the refractive index?
items.e: n = sin i ÷ sin r = sin 25° ÷ sin 10° = 2.43.

items.q: Kevin notices: “Raindrops make a rainbow when the Sun is behind you.” What explains this?
c: Light reflects off a mirror at the same angle.
Sunlight bends and splits into colors inside the drops.
items.e: This is refraction: light changes speed and direction when it enters a new material.

items.q: A ray of light enters a glass block along the normal. What happens to the light?
c: It slows down but does not bend.
It speeds up and bends towards the normal.
It slows down and bends away from the normal.
It slows down and bends towards the normal.
items.e: Light changes speed when it enters a different medium, so it bends (refracts) unless it travels along the normal.

items.q: Kristine notices: “A swimming pool looks shallower than it really is.” What explains this?
c: Light reflects off a mirror at the same angle.
Light from the bottom bends as it leaves the water.
items.e: This is refraction: light changes speed and direction when it enters a new material.

items.q: A ray enters glass (refractive index 1.5) from air and is refracted at 25° to the normal. What was the angle of incidence?
items.e: sin i = n × sin r = 1.5 × sin 25°, so i = 39.3°.

items.q: Light passes from air into crown glass (refractive index 1.52) at an angle of incidence of 20°. What is the angle of refraction?
items.e: sin r = sin 20° ÷ 1.52, so r = 13°.

items.q: A diverging lens forms an image 12 cm on the same side as the object (virtual) when the object is 20 cm away. What is the focal length?
A converging lens has a focal length of 12 cm. An object is 9.6 cm from it. What kind of image is formed?
c: real, inverted and the same size, at 2F on the other side
real, inverted and magnified, beyond 2F on the other side
real, inverted and diminished, between F and 2F on the other side
virtual, upright and magnified, on the same side as the object
items.e: 2F is at 24 cm, so the object is between F and the lens.

items.q: Which device uses a converging lens with the object beyond 2F?
c: a photocopier making a same-size copy
a spotlight making a parallel beam
items.e: Object beyond 2F: image real, inverted and diminished, between F and 2F on the other side.

items.q: A converging lens (f = 12 cm) forms an image of an object placed 15 cm away. What is the magnification? (M = −dᵢ/d₀)
items.e: dᵢ = 60 cm, so M = −dᵢ/d₀ = −(60) ÷ 15 = −4. M is negative: the image is inverted.

items.q: A converging lens (f = 10 cm) forms an image of an object placed 18 cm away. What is the magnification? (M = −dᵢ/d₀)
items.e: dᵢ = 22.5 cm, so M = −dᵢ/d₀ = −(22.5) ÷ 18 = −1.25. M is negative: the image is inverted.

items.q: An object is 45 cm from a diverging lens with a focal length of −30 cm. Use 1/f = 1/d₀ + 1/dᵢ to find the image distance dᵢ.
items.e: 1/dᵢ = 1/f − 1/d₀ = 1/(−30) − 1/45, so dᵢ = −18 cm. A negative dᵢ is a virtual image.

items.q: An object is placed at 2F in front of a thin converging lens. What image is formed?
c: real, inverted and the same size, at 2F on the other side
real, inverted and magnified, beyond 2F on the other side
real, inverted and diminished, between F and 2F on the other side
no clear image: the rays come out parallel (image at infinity)
items.e: Object at 2F: image real, inverted and the same size, at 2F on the other side. Used in a photocopier making a same-size copy.

items.q: A converging lens has a focal length of 12 cm. An object is 24 cm from it. What kind of image is formed?

real, inverted and diminished, between F and 2F on the other side
real, inverted and magnified, beyond 2F on the other side
no clear image: the rays come out parallel (image at infinity)
items.e: 2F is at 24 cm, so the object is at 2F.

items.q: A converging lens has a focal length of 12 cm. An object is 48 cm from it. What kind of image is formed?

items.e: 2F is at 24 cm, so the object is beyond 2F.

items.q: A converging lens (f = 30 cm) forms an image of an object placed 20 cm away. What is the magnification? (M = −dᵢ/d₀)
items.e: dᵢ = −60 cm, so M = −dᵢ/d₀ = −(−60) ÷ 20 = 3. M is positive: the image is upright.

items.q: A diverging lens forms an image 18.8 cm on the same side as the object (virtual) when the object is 50 cm away. What is the focal length?
An object is placed beyond 2F in front of a thin converging lens. What image is formed?
c: real, inverted and the same size, at 2F on the other side

no clear image: the rays come out parallel (image at infinity)

items.e: Object beyond 2F: image real, inverted and diminished, between F and 2F on the other side. Used in a camera.

items.q: An object is 50 cm from a diverging lens with a focal length of −5 cm. Use 1/f = 1/d₀ + 1/dᵢ to find the image distance dᵢ.
items.e: 1/dᵢ = 1/f − 1/d₀ = 1/(−5) − 1/50, so dᵢ = −4.55 cm. A negative dᵢ is a virtual image.

items.q: A diverging lens (f = −20 cm) forms an image of an object placed 30 cm away. What is the magnification? (M = −dᵢ/d₀)
items.e: dᵢ = −12 cm, so M = −dᵢ/d₀ = −(−12) ÷ 30 = 0.4. M is positive: the image is upright.

items.q: An object is placed between F and the lens in front of a thin converging lens. What image is formed?
c: real, inverted and magnified, beyond 2F on the other side
real, inverted and diminished, between F and 2F on the other side
virtual, upright and magnified, on the same side as the object
real, inverted and the same size, at 2F on the other side
items.e: Object between F and the lens: image virtual, upright and magnified, on the same side as the object. Used in a magnifying glass.

items.q: A converging lens (f = 20 cm) forms an image of an object placed 12 cm away. What is the magnification? (M = −dᵢ/d₀)
items.e: dᵢ = −30 cm, so M = −dᵢ/d₀ = −(−30) ÷ 12 = 2.5. M is positive: the image is upright.

items.q: An object is 60 cm from a diverging lens with a focal length of −8 cm. Use 1/f = 1/d₀ + 1/dᵢ to find the image distance dᵢ.
items.e: 1/dᵢ = 1/f − 1/d₀ = 1/(−8) − 1/60, so dᵢ = −7.06 cm. A negative dᵢ is a virtual image.

items.q: An object is 45 cm from a converging lens with a focal length of 15 cm. Use 1/f = 1/d₀ + 1/dᵢ to find the image distance dᵢ.
items.e: 1/dᵢ = 1/f − 1/d₀ = 1/(15) − 1/45, so dᵢ = 22.5 cm. A positive dᵢ is a real image.

items.q: An object is 18 cm from a converging lens with a focal length of 15 cm. Use 1/f = 1/d₀ + 1/dᵢ to find the image distance dᵢ.
items.e: 1/dᵢ = 1/f − 1/d₀ = 1/(15) − 1/18, so dᵢ = 90 cm. A positive dᵢ is a real image.

items.q: An object is 45 cm from a diverging lens with a focal length of −8 cm. Use 1/f = 1/d₀ + 1/dᵢ to find the image distance dᵢ.
items.e: 1/dᵢ = 1/f − 1/d₀ = 1/(−8) − 1/45, so dᵢ = −6.79 cm. A negative dᵢ is a virtual image.

items.q: The speed of sound in air is 332 m/s at 273 K. What is it at 310 K?
A student claps in front of a tall wall and hears the echo 0.1 s later. The speed of sound in air is 340 m/s. How far away is the wall?
items.e: Sound travels to the wall and back: 2d = 340 × 0.1, so d = 17 m.
